project.starter_readme:
My Interactive Art Show - starter

This folder is where your final project begins.

How to start

  1. Open Thonny.
  2. Click File > Open... and open my_art_show.py from this folder.
  3. Click File > Save as... and give your project its own name, for example rainbow_city.py or fish_party.py. Use small letters and underscores, no spaces. Never put your real name in the file name.
  4. Press the green Run button. A window opens with an orange square. That means everything works. Now make it yours!

Remember your plan

Keep your plan sheet (from the project brief) next to the computer. It says:

  • what your program asks the viewer,
  • what it draws,
  • what your function is called and what it draws.

The six ingredients

Your finished program must use all six. The comments at the top of my_art_show.py have a checklist.

Milestones

Tips

  • Work in tiny steps: change one thing, press Run, look, then change the next thing.
  • Save often (Cmd + S).
  • Stuck for more than 5 minutes? Read the red error message out loud to your partner, then ask your teacher. Bugs are normal!
  • Want to see an example of a finished project? Ask your teacher to show you the Night Sky Postcard.

starter_files.html: # My Interactive Art Show # Made by: (write a nickname here - never your real full name) # # My idea in one sentence: # TODO: describe your picture or game here # # My program must use ALL of these ingredients. Check them off as you go: # [ ] input() - asks the viewer at least one question # [ ] a variable - remembers an answer or a number # [ ] an if - chooses what to draw from an answer # [ ] a loop - for ... in range(...): repeats something # [ ] random - adds a surprise # [ ] def - at least one function I made myself # # Work in small steps: change one thing, press Run, look, then change the next. import random import turtle # ===== PART 1: MY COLORS ===== # Color-blind-safe colors. Use these names instead of typing the codes. ORANGE = "#E69F00" SKY_BLUE = "#56B4E9" GREEN = "#009E73" YELLOW = "#F0E442" BLUE = "#0072B2" VERMILLION = "#D55E00" PURPLE = "#CC79A7" BLACK = "#000000" WHITE = "#FFFFFF" # ===== PART 2: SET UP THE SCREEN AND THE TURTLE ===== screen = turtle.Screen() screen.setup(800, 600) # x goes from -400 to 400, y from -300 to 300 screen.title("My Art Show") # TODO: put the name of your artwork here t = turtle.Turtle() t.speed(0) # 0 = fastest t.pensize(2) # ===== PART 3: MY OWN COMMANDS (FUNCTIONS) ===== # This example function draws a square with its bottom-left corner at (x, y). # TODO: change it into YOUR function (a flower, a fish, a robot, a star...) # and give it a name that says what it draws. def my_shape(x, y, color): t.penup() t.goto(x, y) t.setheading(0) t.pendown() t.color(BLACK, color) t.begin_fill() for side in range(4): t.forward(50) t.left(90) t.end_fill() # ===== PART 4: GREET THE VIEWER AND ASK QUESTIONS ===== print("Welcome to my art show!") # TODO: write your own greeting # TODO: ask your first question and keep the answer in a variable. # Example: answer = input("How many fish? ") # fish_count = int(answer) # Remember: never ask for real names, ages, addresses or other private things. # ===== PART 5: MAKE A CHOICE WITH IF ===== # TODO: use if / elif / else to choose something from an answer. # Example: if mood == "happy": # screen.bgcolor(YELLOW) # else: # screen.bgcolor(BLUE) # ===== PART 6: DRAW! USE A LOOP AND RANDOM ===== # This line uses the example function once so you can see it working. # TODO: call YOUR function inside a loop, using random places or colors. # Example: for i in range(5): # x = random.randint(-350, 350) # my_shape(x, 0, PURPLE) my_shape(-25, -25, ORANGE) # ===== PART 7: FINISHING TOUCHES ===== # TODO (optional): write a title on the screen with t.write(...), # hide the turtle with t.hideturtle() print("Thank you for visiting my art show!") turtle.done()

Final project starter: Arcade Game or Art Studio

You get to build your own program! Pick ONE option:

Option Start from What it does now
A. Arcade game game_template.py Arrow keys move a square; touch the coin before the 30-second timer runs out.
B. Art studio art_studio_template.py n draws a new random flower, s saves it to my_design.txt. Loading (l) is your TODO.

Getting started (5 minutes)

  1. In Finder, make a new folder for your project, for example my-project-ada (use your nickname, not your full name).
  2. Copy your template and my_tests.py into that folder.
  3. Rename the template to your game's name, for example space_snack.py. Use lowercase letters and underscores, no spaces.
  4. Open it in Thonny and press the green Run button. Click the turtle window once so it can hear your keys.
  5. Read the TODOs from top to bottom. Do them one at a time and press Run after every small change.

Your project must have

Running your tests

  1. Open my_tests.py. Change the import line to your program's file name (without .py).
  2. Press Run. Every test should say PASSED.
  3. If Thonny says No module named pytest: Tools > Manage packages..., type pytest, click Search, then Install. No account needed.

Tip: put the rules of your program (scores, moving, touching) in small functions that do not use turtle. Those are easy to test.

Stuck?

  • Nothing happens when you press a key: did you call screen.listen()? Did you write onkey(go_left, "Left") without () after go_left?
  • FileNotFoundError: the file does not exist yet. Catch it with try / except FileNotFoundError and start with an empty list.
  • The program freezes: a while loop never ends. Press the red Stop button and check that something inside the loop changes.
  • Ask your partner to be the "rubber duck": explain your code line by line.

starter_files.name: art_studio_template.py
starter_files.html: """MY ART STUDIO - starter template (project option B). Run it first! Click the window, then press: n make a new random design s save the design in my_design.txt (next to this program) l load the saved design (TODO 2 makes this work) Then make it YOUR studio by working through the TODOs. Project checklist - your finished studio needs all of these: [ ] functions with parameters that return values (random_design ...) [ ] a list (PALETTE - TODO 3: a list of designs, a gallery) [ ] a dictionary (each design is a dict) [ ] a while loop (draw_spiral) [ ] a file (save works; TODO 2: make load work) [ ] 3+ tests (my_tests.py) """ import random import turtle from pathlib import Path # Okabe-Ito colors: safe for color-blind viewers. PALETTE = ["#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#F0E442", "#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#CC79A7", "#000000"] # The saved design sits in the same folder as this program. SAVE_FILE = Path(__file__).parent / "my_design.txt" view = {} # the screen and the turtle current = {} # the design on the screen right now # ---------- RULES: pure functions, no turtle. Test them in my_tests.py. def random_design(): """Return a new design: a dictionary of settings.""" # TODO 1: add your own keys, e.g. "background" or "stroke". return { "petals": random.randint(3, 12), "size": random.randint(60, 180), "color": random.choice(PALETTE[:7]), } def design_to_text(design): """Turn a design into text, one "key=value" line per setting.""" lines = [] for key, value in design.items(): lines.append(f"{key}={value}") return "\n".join(lines) + "\n" def text_to_design(text): """The opposite of design_to_text: turn the text back into a dict.""" design = {} # TODO 2: for each line in text.split("\n"): # skip empty lines; split the line at "=" into key and value; # if value.isdigit(), turn it into an int; put it in design[key]. return design # ---------- DRAWING AND KEYS def draw_spiral(t, size): """A small spiral in the middle. It grows WHILE it is smaller than size.""" t.penup() t.goto(0, 0) t.pendown() length = 2 while length < size / 4: t.forward(length) t.left(30) length = length + 1 def draw_design(t, design): """Draw one design: petals in a circle, then a spiral.""" t.clear() t.color(design["color"]) t.pensize(2) for _ in range(design["petals"]): t.penup() t.goto(0, 0) t.pendown() t.circle(design["size"] / 2, 120) # one side of a petal t.left(60) t.circle(design["size"] / 2, 120) # the other side t.left(60 + 360 / design["petals"]) draw_spiral(t, design["size"]) view["screen"].update() def new_design(): current.clear() current.update(random_design()) draw_design(view["artist"], current) def save_design(): with open(SAVE_FILE, "w") as file: file.write(design_to_text(current)) print("Saved to", SAVE_FILE.name) def load_design(): try: with open(SAVE_FILE) as file: design = text_to_design(file.read()) except FileNotFoundError: print("Nothing saved yet - press s first.") return if not design: print("TODO 2: finish text_to_design so loading works.") return current.clear() current.update(design) draw_design(view["artist"], current) def start_studio(): screen = turtle.Screen() screen.setup(600, 600) screen.title("My Art Studio") screen.tracer(0) artist = turtle.Turtle() artist.hideturtle() view.update(screen=screen, artist=artist) screen.onkey(new_design, "n") screen.onkey(save_design, "s") screen.onkey(load_design, "l") # TODO 3: keep a LIST of designs (a gallery) and press g to show them. screen.listen() new_design() if __name__ == "__main__": start_studio() turtle.done()

starter_files.name: game_template.py
starter_files.html: """MY ARCADE GAME - starter template (project option A). Run it first! Click the window, then use the arrow keys to move the square and touch the coin before the time runs out. Then make it YOUR game by working through the TODOs from top to bottom. Project checklist - your finished game needs all of these: [ ] functions with parameters that return values (clamp, is_touching ...) [ ] a dictionary (SETTINGS - add your own keys) [ ] a game loop (game_loop + countdown use ontimer) [ ] a list (TODO 3) [ ] a file (TODO 4: save the high score) [ ] 3+ tests (my_tests.py) """ import random import turtle # Okabe-Ito colors: safe for color-blind players. Use shapes too! PALETTE = ["#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#F0E442", "#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#CC79A7", "#000000"] # TODO 1: change these numbers and see how the game feels. SETTINGS = { "step": 20, # pixels per key press "wall": 270, # the player stays between -wall and +wall "reach": 25, # this close counts as touching "time_limit": 30, # seconds in one game "tick_ms": 50, # milliseconds between game-loop ticks } game = {"score": 0, "time_left": SETTINGS["time_limit"], "running": True} view = {} # the screen and turtles, filled in by setup_window() # ---------- RULES: pure functions, no turtle. Test them in my_tests.py. def clamp(value, low, high): """Return value, but never less than low and never more than high.""" if value < low: return low if value > high: return high return value def is_touching(x1, y1, x2, y2, reach): """True when point (x1, y1) is within reach of point (x2, y2).""" distance = ((x1 - x2) ** 2 + (y1 - y2) ** 2) ** 0.5 return distance <= reach def add_points(score, points): """Return the new score.""" return score + points # TODO 4: write load_high_score(filename) and save_high_score(filename, score). # Hint: look back at your week 7 work. Open with "w" to write. Reading a file # that does not exist yet gives FileNotFoundError - use try/except. # ---------- DRAWING AND KEYS def setup_window(): screen = turtle.Screen() screen.setup(600, 600) screen.title("My Arcade Game") screen.tracer(0) player = turtle.Turtle() player.shape("square") player.color(PALETTE[4]) player.penup() coin = turtle.Turtle() coin.shape("circle") coin.color(PALETTE[0]) coin.penup() hud = turtle.Turtle() hud.hideturtle() hud.penup() screen.onkey(go_left, "Left") screen.onkey(go_right, "Right") screen.onkey(go_up, "Up") screen.onkey(go_down, "Down") screen.listen() view.update(screen=screen, player=player, coin=coin, hud=hud) def move(dx, dy): """Move the player, but keep it inside the walls.""" player = view["player"] wall = SETTINGS["wall"] x = clamp(player.xcor() + dx, -wall, wall) y = clamp(player.ycor() + dy, -wall, wall) player.goto(x, y) def go_left(): move(-SETTINGS["step"], 0) def go_right(): move(SETTINGS["step"], 0) def go_up(): move(0, SETTINGS["step"]) def go_down(): move(0, -SETTINGS["step"]) def place_coin(): wall = SETTINGS["wall"] view["coin"].goto(random.randint(-wall, wall), random.randint(-wall, wall)) def draw_hud(): hud = view["hud"] hud.clear() hud.goto(-280, 260) hud.write(f"Score: {game['score']} Time: {game['time_left']}", font=("Arial", 16, "bold")) def game_loop(): """Runs every tick_ms milliseconds while the game is running.""" if not game["running"]: return player, coin = view["player"], view["coin"] if is_touching(player.xcor(), player.ycor(), coin.xcor(), coin.ycor(), SETTINGS["reach"]): game["score"] = add_points(game["score"], 1) place_coin() # TODO 3: make a LIST of enemies (or extra coins). Move each one here # with a for loop, and check if the player touches it. draw_hud() view["screen"].update() view["screen"].ontimer(game_loop, SETTINGS["tick_ms"]) def countdown(): """Runs once a second: the clock goes down until it reaches 0.""" game["time_left"] = game["time_left"] - 1 if game["time_left"] <= 0: game["running"] = False draw_hud() view["hud"].goto(0, 0) view["hud"].write("TIME UP!", align="center", font=("Arial", 24, "bold")) # TODO 4: save the score here if it is a new high score. # TODO 5: press space to play again. view["screen"].update() else: view["screen"].ontimer(countdown, 1000) def start_game(): setup_window() place_coin() draw_hud() view["screen"].ontimer(game_loop, SETTINGS["tick_ms"]) view["screen"].ontimer(countdown, 1000) if __name__ == "__main__": start_game() turtle.done()

starter_files.name: my_tests.py
starter_files.html: """MY TESTS - open this file in Thonny and press the green Run button (F5). pytest runs every function whose name starts with test_ and tells you which ones PASSED and which FAILED. A test is a small check: assert <something that should be True>, "message if it is not" 1. Change the import below to YOUR program's file name (without .py). 2. Keep the example tests that still fit, delete the others. 3. Write at least 3 tests of YOUR OWN functions (TODO at the bottom). Test a normal case AND an edge case (a wall, zero, an empty list...). """ import art_studio_template as art import game_template as game # ---- Examples for option A (arcade game) def test_clamp_leaves_a_good_value_alone(): assert game.clamp(50, -270, 270) == 50 def test_clamp_stops_at_the_wall(): # Edge case: past the wall on both sides. assert game.clamp(500, -270, 270) == 270, "Should stop at the right wall." assert game.clamp(-500, -270, 270) == -270, "Should stop at the left wall." def test_touching_only_when_close(): assert game.is_touching(0, 0, 10, 10, 25), "These points are close." assert not game.is_touching(0, 0, 100, 0, 25), "These points are far apart." # ---- Example for option B (art studio) def test_design_to_text_makes_one_line_per_setting(): text = art.design_to_text({"petals": 6, "color": "#009E73"}) assert text == "petals=6\ncolor=#009E73\n" # When you have finished TODO 2 in art_studio_template.py, remove the # # signs below: this test checks that saving and loading give back the same # design (a "round trip"). # # def test_text_to_design_undoes_design_to_text(): # design = {"petals": 6, "size": 120, "color": "#009E73"} # assert art.text_to_design(art.design_to_text(design)) == design # ---- TODO: YOUR tests. Copy this pattern: # # def test_what_should_happen(): # result = my_function(some, values) # assert result == what_i_expect, "a helpful message" if __name__ == "__main__": import pytest pytest.main(["-v", __file__])

project.starter_readme:
Build Something Big - starter kit

Pick ONE option and start from its template:

Option Template What already works
(a) Grid game grid_game_template.py a Grid class, a Hero that moves with the arrow keys and collects treasure
(b) Generative art app art_app_template.py Shape and Square classes, a Gallery, click to add shapes, S = save, L = load
(c) Data / AI app data_app_template.py + data/games.csv CSV loading and cleaning, a DataSet class, counting, averages, a bar chart

test_my_project.py has example tests for all three. Keep the ones for your option, delete the rest, and add your own until you have at least 5.

Getting started (once, with your teacher)

  1. Copy this whole starter folder to your Documents folder and rename it, for example dragon-maze (no spaces is easiest in Terminal).
  2. Delete the templates you are not using. Rename yours, for example grid_game_template.py -> dragon_maze.py, and change the import line in test_my_project.py to match.
  3. Open a Terminal from Thonny: menu Tools > Open system shell... (this Terminal knows Thonny's Python, which has pytest installed). Type these lines, pressing Return after each one:
cd ~/Documents/dragon-maze
git init
git add .
git commit -m "Start my project from the starter kit"

That first commit is your first save point.

Git workflow cheat list

Do this loop many times: change a little -> run it -> test it -> commit.

I want to... Type this
go to my project folder cd ~/Documents/dragon-maze
see what changed git status
see the exact lines that changed git diff
choose a file for the next save point git add dragon_maze.py
choose every changed file git add .
make a save point git commit -m "Add a chaser that uses BFS"
see my save points git log --oneline
undo changes I have NOT committed yet git restore dragon_maze.py
run my tests (in Thonny's system shell) python3 -m pytest -q

Good commit messages say WHAT changed, in a few words, starting with a verb:

  • Good: Add Enemy class that inherits from Character
  • Good: Fix hero walking through the right-hand wall
  • Not helpful: stuff, changes, asdf, final final 2

Golden rules:

  • Commit at least once every session, and whenever something works.
  • Never commit secrets: no real names, passwords, addresses or photos.
  • Stay on one branch (the one git made for you). If git prints something that scares you, stop and ask - nothing is lost while it is committed.

starter_files.name: art_app_template.py
starter_files.html: """My Art App - starter template for project option (b). This already works: press Run, click to add shapes, press S to save your picture and L to load it again. Your job is to make it YOURS: new shape classes, a recursive pattern, your own palette. Look for the TODO comments. Before you start, rename this file to a name nobody else uses, for example spiral_studio.py, and change the import in test_my_project.py. """ import json import random import turtle from pathlib import Path SAVE_FILE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "my_art.json" # Okabe-Ito color-blind-safe palette PALETTE = ["#E69F00", "#56B4E9", "#009E73", "#F0E442", "#0072B2", "#D55E00", "#CC79A7", "#000000"] class Shape: """Base class: every shape has a kind, a position, a size and a color.""" kind = "dot" def __init__(self, x, y, size, color): self.x = x self.y = y self.size = size self.color = color def draw(self, pen): pen.goto(self.x, self.y) pen.dot(self.size, self.color) def to_dict(self): """Turn the shape into a dictionary so json can save it.""" return {"kind": self.kind, "x": self.x, "y": self.y, "size": self.size, "color": self.color} class Square(Shape): """A Square IS a Shape (inheritance). It only changes how it draws.""" kind = "square" def draw(self, pen): pen.goto(self.x - self.size / 2, self.y - self.size / 2) pen.color(self.color) pen.pendown() pen.begin_fill() for _ in range(4): pen.forward(self.size) pen.left(90) pen.end_fill() pen.penup() # TODO: add your own shape class, e.g. class Star(Shape). # TODO (algorithm): add a RECURSIVE shape, e.g. a fractal tree or a spiral: # def draw(self, pen): ... calls a helper that calls itself with a # smaller size, and STOPS at a base case (size < 5). SHAPE_CLASSES = {"dot": Shape, "square": Square} # TODO: add your classes here def shape_from_dict(data): """The opposite of to_dict: build the right kind of shape again.""" shape_class = SHAPE_CLASSES[data["kind"]] return shape_class(data["x"], data["y"], data["size"], data["color"]) class Gallery: """A Gallery HAS a list of shapes (composition).""" def __init__(self): self.shapes = [] def add(self, shape): self.shapes.append(shape) def draw_all(self, pen): pen.clear() for shape in self.shapes: shape.draw(pen) # each shape draws itself its own way def save(self, filename): with open(filename, "w", encoding="utf-8") as file: data = [shape.to_dict() for shape in self.shapes] json.dump(data, file, indent=1) def load(self, filename): """Replace the shapes with the ones in the file (if it exists).""" if not Path(filename).exists(): return False with open(filename, encoding="utf-8") as file: self.shapes = [shape_from_dict(data) for data in json.load(file)] return True def main(): gallery = Gallery() pen = turtle.Turtle() pen.hideturtle() pen.penup() screen = turtle.Screen() screen.title("My Art App - click to add, S to save, L to load") screen.tracer(0) def add_shape(x, y): shape_class = random.choice(list(SHAPE_CLASSES.values())) size = random.randint(10, 60) gallery.add(shape_class(x, y, size, random.choice(PALETTE))) gallery.draw_all(pen) screen.update() def save(): gallery.save(SAVE_FILE) def load(): gallery.load(SAVE_FILE) gallery.draw_all(pen) screen.update() screen.onclick(add_shape) screen.onkey(save, "s") screen.onkey(load, "l") screen.listen() add_shape(0, 0) # start with one shape so the window is not empty if __name__ == "__main__": main() turtle.done()

starter_files.name: data_app_template.py
starter_files.html: """My Data / AI App - starter template for project option (c). This already works: press Run to load data/games.csv (made-up games, no personal data), print a summary and draw a bar chart. Your job is to make it YOURS: your own data, more questions, and a simple AI that predicts. Look for the TODO comments. Before you start, rename this file to a name nobody else uses, for example game_guesser.py, and change the import in test_my_project.py. """ import csv import turtle from pathlib import Path DATA_FILE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "data" / "games.csv" NUMBER_COLUMNS = ["players", "minutes", "action", "puzzle", "rating"] BAR_COLORS = ["#0072B2", "#E69F00", "#009E73", "#CC79A7", "#56B4E9", "#D55E00"] def clean_row(row): """Tidy one row: strip spaces, lower-case words, turn numbers into ints. Returns None for an empty row. A blank number becomes None.""" row = {key: (value or "").strip() for key, value in row.items()} if not row["name"]: return None row["genre"] = row["genre"].lower() for column in NUMBER_COLUMNS: row[column] = int(row[column]) if row[column].isdigit() else None return row class DataSet: """A DataSet HAS a list of rows (each row is a dictionary).""" def __init__(self, rows): self.rows = rows def count_by(self, column): """How many rows have each value? e.g. {"action": 5, "puzzle": 5}""" counts = {} for row in self.rows: counts[row[column]] = counts.get(row[column], 0) + 1 return counts def average(self, column): """Average of a number column, ignoring blanks (None).""" values = [row[column] for row in self.rows if row[column] is not None] if not values: return 0 return sum(values) / len(values) def top(self, column, n=3): """The n rows with the biggest value in column (a sort with key=).""" rows = [row for row in self.rows if row[column] is not None] return sorted(rows, key=lambda row: row[column], reverse=True)[:n] def load_dataset(filename): with open(filename, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as file: rows = [clean_row(row) for row in csv.DictReader(file)] return DataSet([row for row in rows if row is not None]) def distance(a, b, features): """How different are two rows? Add up the gaps between their features.""" return sum(abs(a[f] - b[f]) for f in features) # TODO (AI): write nearest_neighbor(dataset, mystery, features) that finds # the row with the SMALLEST distance to the mystery game and returns its # genre. Try mystery = {"action": 5, "puzzle": 1}. Then test it! # TODO (stretch): k-nearest neighbors - let the 3 closest rows vote. def draw_bar_chart(counts, title): """Bars with the label AND the number written on them (not color only).""" pen = turtle.Turtle() pen.hideturtle() pen.penup() width, gap, scale = 60, 20, 40 x = -(len(counts) * (width + gap)) / 2 pen.goto(0, 180) pen.write(title, align="center", font=("Arial", 16, "bold")) for i, (label, count) in enumerate(sorted(counts.items())): pen.goto(x, -150) pen.color("black", BAR_COLORS[i % len(BAR_COLORS)]) pen.pendown() pen.begin_fill() for side in [width, count * scale, width, count * scale]: pen.forward(side) pen.left(90) pen.end_fill() pen.penup() pen.goto(x + width / 2, -175) pen.write(label, align="center", font=("Arial", 12, "normal")) pen.goto(x + width / 2, -145 + count * scale) pen.write(str(count), align="center", font=("Arial", 12, "bold")) x += width + gap turtle.update() def main(): data = load_dataset(DATA_FILE) print(f"Loaded {len(data.rows)} games.") print("Average rating:", round(data.average("rating"), 1)) for row in data.top("rating"): print(f" {row['name']}: {row['rating']}") turtle.tracer(0) draw_bar_chart(data.count_by("genre"), "Games per genre") if __name__ == "__main__": main() turtle.done()

starter_files.name: grid_game_template.py
starter_files.html: """My Grid Game - starter template for project option (a). This already works: press Run and move the hero (H) with the arrow keys. Your job is to turn it into YOUR game. Look for the TODO comments. Before you start, rename this file to a name nobody else uses, for example dragon_maze.py, and change the import in test_my_project.py. """ import turtle CELL = 30 # size of one square in pixels # A level is just text: # = wall, . = floor, H = hero, * = treasure. # TODO: design your own level here (or load it from a file, see save_level). LEVEL = """ ########## #H.....*.# #.####...# #....#.#.# #.*..#.#.# ######...# #*.......# ########## """ class Grid: """A 2D grid of one-letter strings: grid.cells[row][col].""" def __init__(self, text): lines = [line for line in text.strip().splitlines() if line] self.rows = len(lines) self.cols = max(len(line) for line in lines) # ljust pads short rows with walls so every row is the same length self.cells = [list(line.ljust(self.cols, "#")) for line in lines] def in_bounds(self, row, col): return 0 <= row < self.rows and 0 <= col < self.cols def get(self, row, col): return self.cells[row][col] def set(self, row, col, value): self.cells[row][col] = value def find(self, letter): """Return (row, col) of the first square holding letter, or None.""" for row in range(self.rows): for col in range(self.cols): if self.cells[row][col] == letter: return (row, col) return None def count(self, letter): return sum(row.count(letter) for row in self.cells) def is_open(self, row, col): return self.in_bounds(row, col) and self.cells[row][col] != "#" def neighbors(self, row, col): """Open squares next to (row, col): up, down, left, right.""" result = [] for d_row, d_col in [(-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1)]: if self.is_open(row + d_row, col + d_col): result.append((row + d_row, col + d_col)) return result def to_text(self): return "\n".join("".join(row) for row in self.cells) # TODO (saved file): add save_level(filename) and a load_level(filename) # function, so your levels live in .txt files next to this program. class Hero: """The player. TODO: make a base class (for example Character) and let Hero AND a new Enemy class inherit from it (or use composition).""" def __init__(self, row, col): self.row = row self.col = col self.treasure = 0 def move(self, grid, d_row, d_col): """Step one square unless a wall is in the way. True if moved.""" new_row, new_col = self.row + d_row, self.col + d_col if not grid.is_open(new_row, new_col): return False grid.set(self.row, self.col, ".") self.row, self.col = new_row, new_col if grid.get(new_row, new_col) == "*": self.treasure += 1 grid.set(new_row, new_col, "H") return True # TODO (algorithm): add breadth-first search, flood fill or a recursive # function. Idea: an enemy that uses BFS (with collections.deque) to chase H. # ---------------------------------------------------------------- drawing # Shapes AND letters, so the game never depends on color alone. COLORS = {"#": "#0072B2", "*": "#E69F00", "H": "#009E73"} def draw(pen, grid, hero): pen.clear() left = -grid.cols * CELL / 2 top = grid.rows * CELL / 2 for row in range(grid.rows): for col in range(grid.cols): letter = grid.get(row, col) x = left + col * CELL y = top - row * CELL if letter in COLORS: pen.goto(x, y) pen.color("black", COLORS[letter]) pen.begin_fill() for _ in range(4): pen.forward(CELL) pen.right(90) pen.end_fill() if letter in "H*": pen.goto(x + CELL / 2, y - CELL + 6) pen.write(letter, align="center", font=("Arial", 14, "bold")) pen.goto(0, top + 10) pen.write(f"Treasure: {hero.treasure}", align="center", font=("Arial", 14, "bold")) turtle.update() def main(): grid = Grid(LEVEL) row, col = grid.find("H") hero = Hero(row, col) pen = turtle.Turtle() pen.hideturtle() pen.penup() def go(d_row, d_col): hero.move(grid, d_row, d_col) draw(pen, grid, hero) screen = turtle.Screen() screen.title("My Grid Game") screen.tracer(0) screen.onkey(lambda: go(-1, 0), "Up") screen.onkey(lambda: go(1, 0), "Down") screen.onkey(lambda: go(0, -1), "Left") screen.onkey(lambda: go(0, 1), "Right") screen.listen() draw(pen, grid, hero) if __name__ == "__main__": main() turtle.done()

starter_files.name: test_my_project.py
starter_files.html: """Example tests for the three starter templates. 1. Keep the section for the option you chose and delete the other two. 2. When you rename your program, change the import line to match. 3. Add your OWN tests until you have at least 5 (the project needs 5+). A good test: set something up, do ONE thing, then assert what you expect. Run them in Terminal, from your project folder: python3 -m pytest -q """ import sys from pathlib import Path HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE)) # so Python finds the programs in this folder # ---------------------------------------------------------------- option (a) import grid_game_template as game # noqa: E402 (change to your file name) TINY = """ ##### #H.*# ##### """ def test_grid_reads_the_level(): grid = game.Grid(TINY) assert (grid.rows, grid.cols) == (3, 5) assert grid.find("H") == (1, 1) assert grid.count("*") == 1 def test_hero_cannot_walk_through_walls(): grid = game.Grid(TINY) hero = game.Hero(1, 1) assert hero.move(grid, -1, 0) is False, "There is a wall above the hero." assert (hero.row, hero.col) == (1, 1) def test_hero_collects_treasure(): grid = game.Grid(TINY) hero = game.Hero(1, 1) hero.move(grid, 0, 1) hero.move(grid, 0, 1) assert hero.treasure == 1 and grid.count("*") == 0 # ---------------------------------------------------------------- option (b) import art_app_template as art # noqa: E402 def test_gallery_save_and_load_round_trip(tmp_path): gallery = art.Gallery() gallery.add(art.Square(10, 20, 30, "#0072B2")) gallery.add(art.Shape(-5, 0, 12, "#E69F00")) gallery.save(tmp_path / "art.json") copy = art.Gallery() assert copy.load(tmp_path / "art.json") saved = [s.to_dict() for s in gallery.shapes] assert [s.to_dict() for s in copy.shapes] == saved assert isinstance(copy.shapes[0], art.Square), \ "Loading should rebuild the right class." # ---------------------------------------------------------------- option (c) import data_app_template as data_app # noqa: E402 def test_cleaning_skips_empty_rows_and_tidies_text(): data = data_app.load_dataset(data_app.DATA_FILE) assert len(data.rows) == 13, "The empty row should be skipped." assert data.count_by("genre")["action"] == 5, \ "' Action ' should be cleaned to 'action'." def test_average_ignores_blanks(): data = data_app.DataSet([{"rating": 4}, {"rating": None}, {"rating": 2}]) assert data.average("rating") == 3
